workload.text: Matching synthetic short, wrapped, multiline and Unicode bodies
workload.scroll: 80 logical pixels per approximately 16ms, alternating direction every 60 ticks
workload.history_expansion: Preserves recent-row caches; 10000-message scrolling revisits a warm range

method.memory: smaps_rollup captured after idle, scroll-10000 and resize-10000 phase reports; values in KiB. Captures happen just after the next phase begins, rather than stopping the application. RSS/PSS exclude discrete GPU VRAM.
method.graphics_verification: Per-process loaded driver libraries and amdgpu fdinfo at each memory sample. WGPU is compiled with Vulkan as its only native graphics backend. vulkaninfo identifies RADV POLARIS12 on PCI 0000:04:00.0.
method.cpu: Whole-child-process user+system CPU seconds via resource.getrusage(RUSAGE_CHILDREN) differences.
method.diagnostic_feature: unstable-wgpu-30 is necessary to expose BeforeRendering/AfterRendering callbacks on the WGPU surface in Slint 1.18.1; both backends use the same binary.
method.configuration: Standard prebuilt Skia; unchanged upstream dependencies and default cache settings. OpenGL remains the application default. Cargo.toml and Cargo.lock unchanged.

limits: Three measured runs per backend after one warm-up each; small samples from one machine, not a general toolkit or driver guarantee.
p95 frame intervals measure application rendering cadence, not compositor presentation or input-to-photon latency.
Render CPU callbacks exclude WGPU surface acquisition, some synchronization/presentation, and some application/layout work; they are not end-to-end GPU timings.
10000 messages are loaded, but scrolling revisits recent rows; this is not a cold traversal of all messages.
Startup, idle, composer and maximize/restore phases have intentional frame gaps; their frame interval p95 is not a frame-budget comparison.
Memory and DRM sampling adds small identical diagnostic work to both paths; no caches were cleared or tuned.
Native visual correctness, minimize animation, IME, mixed DPI, media and live-account load were not tested.

conclusion.performance: Vulkan consistently improves the small-history scrolling phase in this session (p95 about 17.4–17.7 ms versus 33.0–33.5 ms). Large-history scrolling and resizing are much closer; there is no general twofold speedup.
conclusion.memory: At the end of 10000-message scrolling Vulkan uses about 31 MiB less RSS and 12 MiB less PSS (median-to-median). Shared mapping accounting explains part of the RSS difference. These process metrics exclude GPU VRAM.
conclusion.decision: Retain the current OpenGL default during this comparison. Vulkan is a promising candidate for the next deliberate desktop trial; neither caches nor Skia feature selection were changed.
conclusion.validation: One warm-up per backend and all six measured trials completed without reported renderer errors or fallback; both paths used the same physical GPU.
